strategy.summary: Reproduce the SparseArray._take_with_fill dtype promotion bug (GH#68469) in pandas at buggy commit 1087a91a531b by building pandas from source and running the added sparse indexing and groupby tests; they should fail on the buggy revision (subtype promoted via np.result_type / maybe_promote) and pass on the fixed revision.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang) for building pandas extensions
pinned_because: NumPy: no documented version constraint in the README; left unpinned, so the build uses the current NumPy compatible with this pandas revision. Chosen by this strategy, not by evidence.

numpy 2.5 relevance: the commit note says numpy 2.5 deprecates unitless NaT, which the fix avoids; this is a commit note only, not a pinned requirement, so it is not enforced here. Installing a numpy release that predates or postdates 2.5 is a choice this plan leaves open.
Cython: no documented version; installed unpinned as the README instructs for source installs.
python-dateutil and tzdata: no documented constraint; installed unpinned as dependencies.

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest pandas/tests/arrays/sparse/test_indexing.py pandas/tests/groupby/test_sparse.py -k "preserves_subtype or all_fill or datetimelike or empty or object_subtype or first_last or no_gaps" -q
strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/arrays/sparse/test_indexing.py::test_take_fill_preserves_subtype (parametrized over int8, int32, uint16, uint64, float32); test_take_fill_datetimelike_subtype; test_take_fill_datetimelike_new_fill_is_nat; test_take_fill_empty_preserves_subtype; test_take_fill_empty_datetimelike; test_take_fill_datetimelike_no_gaps; pandas/tests/groupby/test_sparse.py::test_sparse_groupby_first_last_preserves_subtype and test_sparse_groupby_first_last_datetimelike
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 1087a91a531b the listed tests FAIL: identity take with allow_fill=True promotes Sparse[int8,0] to int64, Sparse[uint64,0] to float64 (losing 2**63+12345 precision), datetime64 subtypes to object or datetime64[us], and empty or no-gap datetimelike takes raise DTypePromotionError or return wrong dtype. On the fixed revision (with the _promote_for_fill change) the same tests PASS, with result.dtype.subtype equal to the input subtype and tm.assert_sp_array_equal succeeding.
strategy.numerical_probe: Take [0,1,2] with allow_fill=True from SparseArray([1,0,2**63+12345], dtype=uint64, fill_value=0) and compare the subtype and the exact uint64 value to the input.

input_output_examples.input: arr.take([0, 1, 2], allow_fill=True) with self.dtype Sparse[datetime64[s], Timestamp(...)]

risks: Platform dependence: the uint64 precision loss is a float64 rounding effect, reproducible on any IEEE-754 platform, but the test relies on 2**63+12345 which needs a 64-bit integer type; 32-bit builds may not represent it, so run on a 64-bit Linux or macOS host.
Toolchain: building pandas from source needs a working C compiler and Cython; a mismatched Cython or missing compiler will fail the build before any test runs.

NumPy version: the datetime promotion behaviour depends on the NumPy version (the numpy 2.5 unitless NaT deprecation is only a commit note). If the installed NumPy changes maybe_promote or result_type semantics, buggy and fixed revisions may both pass or both fail; pin NumPy only if the transition does not reproduce.
Tolerance: no tolerance is documented; the tests use exact equality via tm.assert_sp_array_equal, so no tolerance applies.
Sanitisers or alternate architectures are not indicated by the evidence; the defect is a logic/dtype bug not a memory or ARM-specific one, so no special platform is assumed.

The groupby first/last tests route through take only when the array stays sparse; if a pandas version densifies first/last, those tests will not transition and should be treated as secondary to the arrays tests.

The added test file also contains tests that may pass on buggy revision (e.g. object subtype keeps boxed Timestamp, all-fill-all-new), so only the preserves_subtype, datetimelike and empty tests carry the transition.

oracle.reference_source: the developer test assertions via tm.assert_sp_array_equal and dtype equality
oracle.why: Dtype round-trip and exact uint64 values are integer or structural checks; no floating tolerance is stated in the evidence.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On 1087a91a531b the result dtype is promoted (for example Sparse[int64] or Sparse[float64] or Sparse[object] or datetime64[us]), so the dtype equality and assert_sp_array_equal checks fail; the uint64 case also loses precision above 2**53.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With _promote_for_fill keeping the subtype when can_hold_element holds the fill, the result dtype equals the input subtype and assert_sp_array_equal succeeds.
